text.text: Your immigration practice in one place. Start with Notices that need action today or this week, check each Case and its response date, and chase evidence items from clients. Operational tracking only; it holds no legal advice, and the date printed on each notice controls.
Every notice is logged the same day it arrives, read by two people, and given an owner. Requests for evidence and interview notices have fixed dates, and missing one can end a case.

Check every receipt for spelling of names, dates of birth and the right form. Errors are corrected early by request; later they cause delays.

Ask about the full immigration history: entries and exits, every status held, any overstay, prior applications, arrests or charges anywhere. Problems found later are much harder.
Identify the path and any alternative. Explain timelines using current published processing times, not promises.

text.text: Each month, compare clients' priority dates with the published visa bulletin and tell clients whose dates became current. Note the check on the case page.
When an agency deadline is impossible
Contact the attorney immediately. Some deadlines cannot be extended; some can be met with a partial response and a request. Never let a date pass without a decision.

Chen's student status ends in 40 days. His school transfer and visa paperwork are at Intake. The case goes to the top of Monday's list, the attorney reviews it, and the client gets a written plan with the dates.
No open case without a next date
Every notice with an action due has an owner
Every client in temporary status has an expiry date entered
Immigration clients are waiting on decisions that shape their lives. Regular, clear updates in their language prevent anxious calls and build the trust that brings referrals.
Within one business day of any notice, with a copy and a plain explanation.
At least once a month for every open case, even when nothing has changed.
Before any interview, biometrics appointment or filing deadline.
. Use a qualified interpreter or translator, not a family member, for anything important.
Start with what happened, then what it means, then what the client needs to do and by when.
Keep legal terms to a minimum and explain the ones you need.

"Your work petition received a request for more evidence about your job duties. This is common. We need a detailed letter from your employer by the 15th. We will send them a list today. Your case is still active and you can keep working."
Every open case has had contact this month
Clients with status expiring in 120 days know the plan
Clients waiting on documents know exactly what is missing
A denial or a notice of intent to deny is delivered by the attorney, by phone or in person, never by email alone. Explain the options and the time limits for each, then send a written summary.
Tell every client with a pending case, in writing, whether they may travel. Travel during some pending applications can abandon them.
Send the approval, explain what comes next (cards in the mail, when to apply for the next step, such as removing conditions or naturalization) and set the future date on the case page.
Jocelyn's parent petition was approved over a year ago. The attorney's closing letter explained the consular processing steps and set a check-in for when the visa interview is scheduled.

The case office of an immigration practice: each client's cases by form, every notice that arrives from the agency, the evidence still to collect, and the dates that cannot be missed. Filings themselves stay in your forms software and document system.
